q: In an overhead service, where do the service-entrance conductors enter their raceway on the building?
o: At the pull box of the lateral
ref: Stein et al., Mechanical and Electrical Equipment for Buildings (electric service); PEC 2017 Art. 2.30
n: The overhead service drop ends at the building, and the service-entrance conductors turn down into conduit through a service head (weatherhead). The head faces down and sits above the point of attachment, with drip loops, so rain cannot run into the conduit.

q: What equipment lowers the distribution voltage to the utilization voltage delivered to a building?
ref: Stein et al., Mechanical and Electrical Equipment for Buildings (electric service); PEC 2017 Art. 2.30
n: The distribution transformer, pole-mounted or pad-mounted near the user, reduces the primary distribution voltage to service levels such as 230 V or 400/230 V. The substation transformer works one stage earlier, on transmission voltage.

q: At what point does electric power enter the utility supply chain?
ref: Stein et al., Mechanical and Electrical Equipment for Buildings (electric service); PEC 2017 Art. 2.30
n: Power is produced at the generating station (hydro, thermal, geothermal, solar and so on). Every later stage only moves it or changes its voltage: transmission lines carry it, substations step it down, and distribution circuits deliver it.

q: Building electrical components fall into three categories. Which category do conductors, conduits and cable trays belong to?
ref: Stein et al., Mechanical and Electrical Equipment for Buildings (electric service); PEC 2017 Art. 2.30
n: The three categories are wiring and raceways (conductors and what encloses them), power-handling equipment (switchboards, panelboards, transformers, breakers), and utilization equipment (the loads that use the power).

q: In an underground service entrance, where are the underground service conductors brought?
o: Up to a service head on the roof
To the nearest utility pole only
Straight to a branch-circuit panel without metering
ref: Stein et al., Mechanical and Electrical Equipment for Buildings (electric service); PEC 2017 Art. 2.30
n: In an underground service (service lateral) the conductors run buried in conduit from a pole riser or a pad-mounted transformer and come up to the meter socket. After the meter they continue to the main breaker.

q: Switchboards, panelboards, transformers and circuit breakers fall under which category of building electrical components?
ref: Stein et al., Mechanical and Electrical Equipment for Buildings (electric service); PEC 2017 Art. 2.30
n: Power-handling equipment controls, protects, transforms and distributes power but does not use it. Conductors and conduits are wiring and raceways, and the loads are utilization equipment.

q: What are the smaller lines that branch off a main distribution circuit to serve a small group of customers?
ref: Stein et al., Mechanical and Electrical Equipment for Buildings (electric service); PEC 2017 Art. 2.30
n: Tap lines (laterals) branch from the main distribution feeder into side streets and small customer clusters, usually through a fuse cutout so a fault on the tap does not trip the whole feeder.

q: Why is an underground service often chosen over an overhead service?
o: No exposed wires, so it is safer and neater
It is always cheaper to install
It needs no electric metering at all
It avoids the need for a main disconnect
ref: Stein et al., Mechanical and Electrical Equipment for Buildings (electric service); PEC 2017 Art. 2.30
n: Underground service removes the aerial drop, so typhoon winds, falling branches and accidental contact are less of a risk, and the facade looks cleaner. It costs more for trenching, conduit and repair access. It still needs a meter and a main disconnect.

q: What carries bulk power at high voltage from generating plants toward distant load centers?
ref: Stein et al., Mechanical and Electrical Equipment for Buildings (electric service); PEC 2017 Art. 2.30
n: Transmission lines run at very high voltages (69 kV to 500 kV on the Philippine grid) because a higher voltage means less current and so less I²R loss over long distances. Distribution circuits come later and run at lower voltages near the users.

q: What are the utility circuits that run along roads to serve neighborhoods, businesses and other customers?
ref: Stein et al., Mechanical and Electrical Equipment for Buildings (electric service); PEC 2017 Art. 2.30
n: Distribution circuits (primary feeders) leave the substation and follow streets to reach communities. Branch circuits are different: they are the final circuits inside a building, after the panelboard.

q: Lighting fixtures, motors and appliances fall under which category of building electrical components?
ref: Stein et al., Mechanical and Electrical Equipment for Buildings (electric service); PEC 2017 Art. 2.30
n: Utilization equipment is where electric energy is finally used, turned into light, motion or heat. It sits at the end of the chain, after the wiring and the power-handling equipment.

q: How does an overhead service entrance bring power into a building?
o: Aerial conductors run from the pole to the building
Buried conductors in conduit run from the pole to the meter
Power is generated on site and fed straight to the panel
Conductors run through the foundation from a street vault
ref: Stein et al., Mechanical and Electrical Equipment for Buildings (electric service); PEC 2017 Art. 2.30
n: In an overhead service the service drop spans through the air from the utility pole to a point of attachment on the building. From there the service-entrance conductors run through the service head and the meter to the main disconnect.

q: Which facility steps transmission voltage down and switches power among outgoing distribution circuits?
ref: Stein et al., Mechanical and Electrical Equipment for Buildings (electric service); PEC 2017 Art. 2.30
n: A substation houses transformers, breakers and switchgear. It lowers the transmission voltage to a distribution voltage (such as 13.2 kV or 34.5 kV) and splits the power among the feeders that leave it.
